facts.fact: The vendor's comparison table lists the CTV cost range as $15-$35 CPM.
facts.quote: Cost (CPM range) | $15-$35 | $5-$25

facts.fact: The vendor states that a 30-second video is the CTV creative requirement, and 6-30 second native-style video is the social requirement.
facts.quote: Creative requirements | 30-second video, broadcast-quality | 6-30 sec video, native style

facts.fact: The vendor claims well-targeted CTV campaigns produce foot traffic lifts of 12-30% for local businesses with physical locations.
facts.quote: Local businesses with physical locations consistently see foot traffic lifts of 12-30% during well-targeted CTV campaigns.

facts.fact: The vendor states that below $500/month, Meta typically produces more measurable activity than CTV.
facts.quote: Below $500/month, Meta typically produces more measurable activity than CTV.

facts.fact: The vendor states that CTV's strength shows up at $800 or more per month, when meaningful local frequency becomes achievable.
facts.quote: CTV's strength shows up at $800+/month when meaningful local frequency becomes achievable.

facts.fact: The vendor says Meta lets advertisers test 4-6 creative variations in a week, while CTV testing typically requires 2-4 week windows for a statistically meaningful read.
facts.quote: Meta lets you test 4-6 creative variations in a week with hard data. CTV testing typically requires longer windows (2-4 weeks)

facts.fact: The vendor states that most strong Meta conversions happen within the first 72 hours.
facts.quote: most strong Meta conversions happen within the first 72 hours.

facts.fact: The vendor claims the Meta ad conversion rate rises 15-40% during active CTV flights compared to non-flight periods.
facts.quote: The conversion rate on the Meta ad rises by 15-40% during active CTV flights compared to non-flight periods.

facts.fact: The vendor claims viewers exposed to both CTV and social creative convert at rates 2-3x higher than viewers exposed to only one channel.
facts.quote: viewers exposed to both convert at rates 2-3x higher than viewers exposed to only one channel.

facts.fact: For budgets under $1,000/month, the vendor recommends leaning toward Meta and adding small-budget CTV of $200-$400/month only after Meta is producing reliable results.
facts.quote: consider adding small-budget CTV ($200-$400/month) as a supplemental layer only after Meta is producing reliable results.

facts.fact: For budgets of $1,000-$2,500/month, the vendor suggests a 60/40 Meta/CTV split or 50/50 as a starting point.
facts.quote: A 60/40 Meta/CTV split or even 50/50 is often the right starting point.

facts.fact: For budgets of $2,500-$5,000/month, the vendor recommends a split of typically 40-50% Meta and 40-50% CTV, with the remainder in Google search and other channels.
facts.quote: Balanced split, typically 40-50% Meta, 40-50% CTV, with the remainder in Google search and other supporting channels.

facts.fact: For budgets of $5,000+/month, the vendor suggests 30-40% Meta, 40-50% CTV, with the rest in Google and other channels.
facts.quote: Many small businesses at this scale shift to 30-40% Meta, 40-50% CTV, with the rest in Google and other channels.

facts.fact: The vendor describes a meaningful share of homeowner-age households aged 40+ as using social media lightly while watching substantial streaming TV.
facts.quote: A meaningful share of homeowner-age households (40+) use social media lightly but watch substantial streaming TV.

facts.fact: For local service businesses (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, roofing), the page recommends a 45-55% CTV budget split.
facts.quote: Recommended split: 45-55% CTV, 30-40% Meta, balance in Google.

facts.fact: For retail and e-commerce, the page recommends a 50-60% Meta budget split.
facts.quote: Recommended split: 50-60% Meta, 30-40% CTV, balance in Google.

facts.fact: For restaurants and hospitality, the page recommends a 45-50% Meta budget split.
facts.quote: Recommended split: 45-50% Meta, 35-45% CTV, balance in local platforms.

facts.fact: For professional services, the page recommends a 35-45% LinkedIn/Meta budget split.
facts.quote: Recommended split: 35-45% LinkedIn/Meta, 35-45% CTV, balance in Google.

facts.fact: For healthcare practices, the page recommends a 40-50% CTV budget split.
facts.quote: Recommended split: 40-50% CTV, 30-40% Meta, balance in Google and local SEO.

facts.fact: For fitness studios and wellness businesses, the page recommends a 45-55% Meta budget split.
facts.quote: Recommended split: 45-55% Meta, 30-40% CTV, balance in local platforms.

facts.fact: For wedding and event venues, the page recommends a 35-45% Meta budget split.
facts.quote: Recommended split: 35-45% Meta, 30-40% CTV, balance in directories.

facts.fact: The page recommends a pre-campaign baseline period of 4-6 weeks without CTV running, with Meta at steady spend, for measuring combined channel lift.
facts.quote: Compare total inquiries, sales, or conversions during the combined CTV + Meta window against the pre-campaign baseline (4-6 weeks without CTV running, with Meta at steady spend).

facts.fact: Adwave claims its three-layer measurement framework captures 80-95% of true combined channel impact for small businesses, versus 50-70% with direct attribution alone.
facts.quote: this three-layer measurement framework captures 80-95% of the true combined channel impact, compared to 50-70% with direct attribution alone.

facts.fact: Adwave advises holding Meta spend steady while testing CTV for 60-90 days rather than cutting Meta to fund CTV.
facts.quote: The cleanest approach is to hold Meta steady while testing CTV for 60-90 days.

facts.fact: Adwave describes a clean 90-day comparison of TV and social results as the most defensible read on performance.
facts.quote: A clean 90-day comparison is the most defensible read.

facts.fact: Per the page, cross-channel lift signals such as branded search and Meta CTR rising often appear in the first 2-3 weeks after a CTV launch alongside steady Meta.
facts.quote: Cross-channel lift signals (branded search rising, Meta CTR rising) often appear in the first 2-3 weeks after CTV launches alongside steady Meta.

facts.fact: Per the page, total conversion lift over baseline becomes measurable in 4-6 weeks.
facts.quote: Total conversion lift over baseline becomes measurable in 4-6 weeks.

facts.fact: The page states a very small business with $500-$800 per month total ad budget can run both channels, but typically with most budget on Meta.
facts.quote: Can a very small business ($500-$800/month total) run both channels?

facts.quote: the cost of CTV has dropped dramatically (Adwave runs from $30 a day)

facts.fact: The page gives an illustrative example of Meta at 4x ROAS rising to 4.8x ROAS with CTV added, while CTV produces its own 2-4x direct ROAS.
facts.quote: If your Meta is at 4x ROAS and adding CTV pushes it to 4.8x ROAS while CTV produces its own 2-4x direct ROAS

facts.fact: The page states CTV creative is 30 seconds long, while Meta creative is 6-30 seconds long.
facts.quote: CTV creative is 30 seconds, broadcast-quality, lean-back grammar. Meta creative is 6-30 seconds, native-style, scroll-stopping grammar.

facts.fact: The page says last-click reports can miss earlier ad exposure, so TV and social results should be compared together over a consistent period such as 90 days.
